mission: Three hands linked. Three Force traditions colliding. The sound of it in the Force is three instruments playing in different keys. Ben's instinct is to lead — harmonise the three notes by will. The resonance resists. The discordance worsens. Veraine's ritual builds; Torin's void expands; the trio is falling apart.
why_now: The climax cannot work until Ben has failed to command it. The chapter closes on failure so Ch25 can open on the breakthrough the failure has earned.
conflict: The three traditions are structurally incompatible when one of them tries to dominate. Ben reaches to impose order the way twenty-eight years have trained him to. The resonance does the thing the book has been promising — it refuses to be led.
turning_point: Ben's instinct fires and the resonance worsens in response. The scene ends with the discordance at its peak and the answer still one step away.
opening_hook: Three hands linked. Three Force traditions touching. The sound of it — in the Force — is like three instruments playing in different keys simultaneously.
closing_hook: It's not working. The discordance is worsening. Veraine's ritual is building power. Torin's void is expanding. And the resonance is falling apart. Ben is trying too hard. He's leading when he should be listening.
emotional_trajectory: Determined attempt -> frustration at failure -> the recognition that control is the problem

stakes.personal: The last stand of Ben's reflex to command
stakes.interpersonal: Three people failing to harmonise because one of them is pulling for a lead
stakes.external: The other two operations continuing while theirs stalls

setting: Veranthos — mid-valley, hands linked, the Scar visible, the valley in chaos
sensory_details: The discordance — three Force textures colliding without combining; Sera's tradition rigid and defined, Kael's fluid and sharp, Ben's pulling to harmonise them by will; sweat at his temples, the wound pressing, three keys refusing to resolve
action_beats: Ben links hands with Sera and Kael and the three Force traditions collide — discordant, unstable, wrong
Ben tries to lead the resonance by force of will and feels it resist — his control instinct sabotaging the harmony
Sweat rolls down Ben's temples as the discordance worsens and the other two operations grow stronger around them
notes: Failure-before-success is the engine of the climax. Do not let the resonance start to cohere in this scene — the discordance holds through the closing. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, articulate to himself that control is the problem. The reader recognises it through the shape of the failure; Ben's recognition is Ch25's work. Anti-pattern: do not use 'it was as if the Force had —' constructions during the resonance; the vocabulary is three notes, three keys, three currents, not simile-cascades. One consistent acoustic image per paragraph.
